findings.reason: an implementer following the stated rule literally returns 1 and fails the section's own failing-at-base case, and the only thing that would catch it is that case, which is then the temptation to weaken.
findings.text: the What-changes says `launch_reservation_key` "answers the newest receipt plus one only when a receipt exists" and that "with only the marker, the launch keeps the attempt it was dispatched with", but the function (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2218`) reads only `attempt_receipt_numbers` and the canonical `worker.json`/`exit.json`, and returns `1` when none exists — the marker `attempt.json` is written at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2774`, before the reservation block at `:2856`, and carries the dispatched attempt, yet the plan never says the key reads it, so the paired shadow arm's first launch gets attempt 1 rather than its dispatched 2

findings.reason: it is a labelling error in the record, not a mechanism error; the exit-receipt sub-case does fail at base and carries the measure.
findings.text: the Done-when opens "each behaviour change has a case that fails at the dispatch base and passes at the head", but the (3) sub-case "when the supervisor rewrite fails, the reservation still refuses a second launch while the worker runs" holds at base too, since base `held_launch_reservation` already refuses on a live admitting process, so the blanket claim misdescribes which cases carry the failing-at-base control

findings.reason: the done-when already pins the fixture that makes the point (a node with an earlier committed run, so attempt 2 or more), so no node builds the wrong case from it.
findings.text: defect (1) says the shadow arm's attempt is "derived from the primary line", but a paired shadow arm has `paired_masks` set, so the primary-line branch at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2737` does not run and the attempt comes from the node's own prior committed runs at `:2746`–`:2759`
